analysis:
Examined all supplied units and change orientation against the canonical index and selected T-041 detail. release-provider.yml:941-977 adds final-artifact cluster fact computation, deleting the signing keychain and checking identity removal before invoking the new script. It verifies the bundle hash before extraction. Lines 1078-1088 attach facts only when CLUSTER_RUNTIME_SEND is true; computation failure blocks that enabled path, while disabled lanes retain advisory results without changing the payload. Existing signature, entitlement, notarization and artifact identity checks remain visible and outside the changed ranges. release-swift.yml:66-67 only expands staging trigger paths; environment selection and permissions are unchanged. No concrete regression is established by these excerpts.
Integration must examine scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-facts.sh, scripts/provider-cluster-runtime-models.py and provider-release-publication.py together: verify actual subprocess environment isolation (not merely comments), fact validation and binding to the exact signed artifact, and that runtime self-reports cannot substitute for independent qualification or serving authorization (A-005, A-011, A-017, T-054, T-056, TB-011). These implementations are not supplied here.
The changelog patch describes excluding coordinator registration timeouts from pair failure counts and retrying a set-aside pair after one hour using the same approval. This is evidence of intended behavior, not implementation proof. Integration must check the changed pair lifecycle code for current approval expiry/revocation, connection binding and admission checks on retry (A-016, T-053), plus availability effects (A-018). The changelog unit itself supplies metadata only; its text was examined through file_changes. No cache, prompt encryption, billing or fan-authority control changes are demonstrated in this scope. Missing runtime and publication source leaves material security contracts unresolved, not presumed safe.
